note: Pass 2. The compare step mis-paired D9/D10: r1-28 (متأكتي, 20:57) was paired with r2-34 (إلي→إنو, 21:01) while r1-29 is the same إلي→إنو row - so إلي→إنو was in fact found by BOTH readers; it is settled once under D10 (high) and D9 carries only the متأكتي piece. D22 is kept but re-labelled: the transcript shows a wrong VERB (صلح for ساعد, he fixed to ساعدني after her prompt at 11:02), not a D3 preposition-ending error - the merger should check whether an agreed row already covers 10:34 صلاحني→ساعدني and dedupe. One added row (53:14 تعبي→تبعي) may also duplicate an agreed row; match by t and wrong. Lesson-wide: ASR badly garbles his Arabic in this file (Next far, take Allah, Dan's, بتداي), so several B rows are low; his D1-style letter swaps (زعمت/عزمت, تعبي/تبعي) are ruled tier-1 vocab because they produce a different real word that Amal treated as wrong, not as a slip.

row.why: He said زعمت (I claimed) three times in a row (02:49, 02:56, 02:59) for عزمت (I invited; sheet: i invited | Ana 3azamet | أنا عزمت); Amal first made him retry (جرّب كم مرة) then recast عزمت, and he himself flags it as a corrected word at 04:05 - a consistent different real word, not a one-off S4 slip, so tier 1 not tier 2.

rulings.why: Both readers agree on the slip; tier 1 fits: زعم is a different lexical item, not a wrong form of عزم, and she treated it as an error (retry prompt then recast).

row.why: Her sheet fixes the preposition on this verb (i call | Ana barenn (3ala) | أنا برن); he used لـ; she let it pass while they hunted the word for electrician (08:39-09:10); low because رنّ لـ is also heard colloquially and she did not react.

rulings.why: Real per her own sheet (3ala), unflagged by Amal, so grammar-B low; not a duplicate.

row.medi_said: كراجي. This is a new word. It's not gonna be on the list.
row.why: Amal volunteered كهربجي at 09:10; he said it right once (09:13) then reproduced it as كراجي (garage-man, a different word) at 09:30, 09:39 and 09:48, and she recast كهـ، كهربجي syllable by syllable at 09:42 - he attempted the word and got it wrong, so a recast fix (tier 1), not a didn't-know; low stakes because the word was 30 s old and not on her sheet.

rulings.why: Tier 0 is for a word he never attempted or asked for; here he produced a wrong word and she recast it, so tier 1 recast.

row.medi_said: اه، this is take Allah بيتي.
row.why: Telling her he stayed home (ضليت, ASR 'دولت'/'take Allah') he said بيتي with no preposition; she prompted 'بِ أو فِي بيتي؟' and he fixed to بي بيتي at 12:50; medium because his line is ASR-garbled.

rulings.why: Transcript shows the prompt and his fix; real grammar row only r1 wrote.

row.right: عشان الـ air conditioning كان (خربان) / عشان في (my reading)
row.why: Reason for staying home was the broken AC he described at 07:46 and again at 53:29 (عشان الـ air conditioning كان خربان); يكون (subjunctive 'be') has no place here - either في (there is) or كان (was); Amal moved on to شو بتتذكر; low because the clause was left unfinished; 'air conditioning' is not on her sheet so no tier-3.

rulings.why: Wrong ykoon in a plain statement, unflagged; kept low because the sentence is a fragment.

row.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
row.why: 'Two verbs' needs the dual فعلين, he said فعل + تنين; her reply is transcribed 'بس فعلاً', which is not a fix as written - it may be an ASR-garbled 'بس فعلين' (same 'بس X' recast shape as her 'بس كلمة وحدة' 2 s earlier) but the transcript cannot prove it, so B for Amal to confirm.

rulings.why: Both saw the slip; the transcript does not show a clear voiced fix (فعلاً), so grammar-B low rather than grammar-A.

Not a produced error: at 14:19 he asked an English meta question ('What is the preposition here? Is it ... takes be?') and Amal answered it (no preposition; من for 'annoyed with'); no Arabic sentence with a wrong preposition was spoken, so it is a didn't-know question, not a fix of his speech.

row.why: Asking her to repeat بدك نشوف الواجب أو ناخد الفعل الجاي (16:33) he said كم مرة (how many times) for كمان مرة (sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة); she just rephrased the question (16:41); the same rendering recurs at 25:38 while ASR writes كمان correctly elsewhere (43:58, 57:03), so not an ASR drop.
row.english: one more time? / say that again?

rulings.why: Real let-pass vocab slip, consistent across two moments; kept medium.

row.why: 'Are you (f) sure' is the feminine participle متأكدة (sheet: sure / certain | Mit2akked | متأكد); he gave it a verb-like -ti ending; Amal only addressed اللي in this sentence (21:27-21:37); low because ASR may have mis-rendered the ending.

rulings.why: r1's piece is real and unflagged, kept low; r2's piece in this D (إلي→إنو) is the same row as D10 and is settled there - the pairing was a compare artefact.

row.why: 'Sure THAT you didn't annoy him' takes the complementizer إنو; he used the relative اللي; Amal asked 'Why اللي؟' (21:27) then said 'إنو مش اللي' (21:35) and he said 'Oh, whoops'.
row.english: (are you sure) that you (pl) didn't annoy him

rulings.why: Both readers actually found this row (r1-29 and r2-34); explicit fix in the transcript; high.

Cannot be verified: the detached 'أزد هم' (24:25, 24:28) is an ASR spacing artefact - spoken قصدهم with the suffix is what 'azd-hom' sounds like, and مش قصدهم is correct; Amal's 'No' at 24:37 answers his tense question, not this word.

row.why: Second occurrence: asked to repeat زي ما حكينا هديك المرة (25:29) he said كم مرة (how many times) for كمان مرة (sheet: one more time | Kaman marra | كمان مرة); she simply repeated زي ما حكينا and switched to English.
row.english: one more time? / say that again?

rulings.why: Separate moment from D8 (not a duplicate), same let-pass slip; kept medium.

row.medi_said: and to remove his, uh, شول، فيل،

rulings.why: Both saw it; transcript shows an attempt (not a question) at a sheet word she then supplied, so tier 1.

row.medi_said: Next far. Is it next far?
row.amal_said: So it's either inكسر or انكسر.
row.why: Asked for the past (ماضي, 36:38) of the in-verb بنكسر he offered a form ASR wrote as 'Next far' (most likely نكسر without the initial alef); Amal recast the past as انكسر (with the 'in-' onset) and he repeated انكسر at 37:05; low because his exact form is unrecoverable from the transcript.

rulings.why: He produced an Arabic verb form (not a meta question) and she recast it; real but his line is ASR garbage, so low.

row.medi_said: conditioning, air conditionery. Do I say for air condition?
row.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'my air conditioning' and she supplied the تبعي possessive with el- on the noun; he echoed it as تباين (48:31) which she let pass; neither 'air conditioning' nor تبع is on her sheet, so tier 0.

rulings.why: Clear asked/supplied exchange in the transcript; tier 0 didn't-know.

row.why: Answering her يلا بشوفك (see you) he said ما شوفتك (I didn't see you): a negated past where the b-present بشوفك is needed; she just said باي; low because the ASR may have mis-heard a mumbled بشوفك / منشوفك.

rulings.why: Both saw it; the piece he needed is the b-present (B1), the form he used was a past (B5 as bucket2).

S4 sound shape (F2/F3): صلاحتو vs صلحته is the same verb صلّح with the vowel length / shadda wrong (recurs as صلاحني, صلاحلي at 10:34-10:40 and Amal still heard it as صلح, 11:02); the -و/-ه ending is only ASR spelling of the same 3ms suffix; pronunciation, never vocab or grammar.

Not an error and not a didn't-know: at 42:00 he produced the word himself ('Is it إيد's hand, right?' - ASR 'Dan's') and Amal only confirmed (ASR 'ear. مهم'); he then used إيدها correctly at 42:53; she supplied nothing.

Cannot be verified - transcript hole/garble: 'الليلة جو كتير كتير' is a broken ASR line (الليلة جو is a plausible mis-hearing of اليوم الجو, and the adjective may simply be lost); Amal's عن جد؟ reacts to the content (very hot), not the form; no defensible wrong piece.

S4 letter slip / ASR: قربان for خربان at 07:46 is a single ق/خ substitution; he knows the word and said خربان correctly three times later (48:58, 50:12, 53:20); Amal's هييي reacts to the news; pronunciation, not vocab.

Self-fix before help: at 06:40 he said 'tisa asha. Oh no, that's right. Yeah, asha tisa' - he landed on the day-first order himself before Amal's 'First we say عشرة تسعة' (06:42), which restates his fixed version.

row.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
row.why: He meant 'he helped me a bit' (10:40 'helps to me') but used the verb صلح (fix) - a different word; Amal explained صلحني = he fixed me, then prompted 'did you wanna say he helped me?' and he fixed to ساعدني (11:07, 'Oops'); the D3 reading (صلح لي vs صلحني) is moot because the -ني object is right for his intended verb ساعد.

rulings.why: Real fix she voiced, but the transcript supports a wrong-verb vocab row (صلح for ساعد), not the D3 preposition-ending row r2 wrote; merger should dedupe against any agreed 10:34 row.
Not an error: her own sheet gives بلبس for both senses (i wear / i'm putting on | Balbes | بلبس), Amal accepted اليوم بلبس and went on with the colours; لابس is a nicety she has not taught as a rule.

S5 mid-drill stumble: 'هي هو uh, بينكسري' was said before he had picked the subject; Amal did not treat it as a form but redirected to إنتو, and the هي/هو forms were then produced and fixed at 45:34-45:46 (هو بينكسر, هي بتنكسر), which covers the same drill step.
